ready1_open_rewrite.title: GeoSQA Open-ended Question-1
ready1_open_rewrite.rewritten_question_text: The figure below schematically shows Norway's location and terrain. Norway is one of the countries in the world where hydropower resources have been relatively fully developed. Most of this country's large hydropower stations are high-head (the height difference between the water level of the power station reservoir and the location of the generating units is large) power stations. <image1> According to the figure, most of Norway's large hydropower stations are high-head power stations. From the perspective of terrain conditions, what kind of terrain characteristics does this country have?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, Norway's territory is long and narrow, and the contour lines and mountainous relief along the western and southern coastal areas are relatively obvious, with not many flat areas. Reasoning: The question stem states that high-head power stations require a large height difference between the reservoir water level and the location of the generating units; areas with widespread mountains and large terrain relief can easily form this kind of height difference. Therefore, from the perspective of terrain conditions, Norway has the characteristics of many mountainous areas and large terrain relief.
